answer: A sybil defence is per-identity capital bonding with slashing. Each agent must lock a ferrous-hard stake before it may attest or earn; the bond stays locked while the identity is active and is forfeited when peers catch it double-signing. Registering ten thousand fake agents therefore costs ten thousand real bonds, and the attacker reaches their nadir of profit only after burning that capital. Honest operators recoup the cost through fees, like a single orchard that yields only when tended, so forging identities becomes a structurally losing trade instead of a free multiplication of votes.
